key_insight: Full difference-frequency QTF loading improves floating wind turbine response predictions most consistently, especially for wave-driven low-frequency surge and mooring loads.
engineering_relevance: Including second-order wave loads can improve platform-motion and mooring-load assessments, although their relative importance depends on operating wind conditions.
method: Develop an efficient time-domain full-QTF formulation using bandwidth truncation.
Integrate it into a fully coupled IEA 15 MW turbine–VolturnUS-S platform model.
Compare linear excitation, Newman's approximation, and full-QTF predictions.
evidence_signal: Comparisons with 1:70-scale hybrid wave-basin experiments under wave-only and turbulent wind–wave conditions showed full-QTF surge standard deviation discrepancies below 18% in the most energetic wave conditions, with smaller discrepancies for heave, pitch, and mooring tensions.
watch_item: The reported validation covers one turbine–platform configuration at model scale, so generalization to other systems and full-scale conditions requires further evaluation.
paper_title: Second-order difference-frequency effects on floating wind turbine responses: full-QTF modelling and experimental comparison
